home_ext_does_instagram: Reels, the Explore grid and the suggested accounts are hidden. Your feed, stories, messages, search and your profile stay.
home_ext_does_x: The For you tab, the trends and the news box are hidden. The Following feed, search, notifications and messages stay.

home_faq_free_a1: **Yes.** The Mac app, the browser extension and the manual guide are all free. No account, no payment.
home_faq_free_a2: I do not charge for it. I want people to take addictive feeds off their phones. If it helps you, you can support the work. You never have to.
home_faq_screen_time_a1: **Screen Time has an Ignore Limit button.** When you are tired, you tap it.
home_faq_screen_time_a2: This has no button. Once the profile is locked, you cannot bring the blocked apps and their websites back on the iPhone.
home_faq_supervision_a1: **A mode Apple built for school and company iPhones.**
home_faq_supervision_a2: A supervised iPhone accepts settings a normal one refuses: it can hide apps, and it can keep a profile that cannot be removed on the phone. Everything else about the phone stays the same.
home_faq_needs_a1: **A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14 or later**, for a few minutes, and an iPhone on iOS 26 or older.
home_faq_needs_item_friend: A friend's Mac works too. Delete the app when you are done.
home_faq_needs_item_phone: Your iPhone needs no app, and no Mac afterwards.
home_faq_needs_item_copy: Nothing of your iPhone stays on the Mac afterwards.
home_faq_ios27_a1: **Not yet.** On iOS 27 the app cannot supervise the iPhone, and the iPhone can be erased. Do not run it on iOS 27.
home_faq_ios27_a2: Supervise it by hand with Apple Configurator instead. The {guide} shows each step. That way erases the iPhone.
home_faq_ios27_a3: From its next version, the app checks the iOS version and tells you the same.
home_faq_data_a1: **Back up first.** In our tests on iOS 26 and older, the app kept apps, photos and messages. If something goes wrong, the backup is the way back. **We are not responsible for lost data.**
home_faq_data_finder_connect: connect the iPhone to your Mac
home_faq_data_changes: **What changes:** only the apps you block disappear.
home_faq_time_a1: **A few minutes.** The app sends a small set of settings to the iPhone in seconds. Then the iPhone restarts, which takes about 3 minutes. When it is back, unlock it, tap Trust and enter your passcode.
home_faq_fail_a1: **The app tells you what stopped and how to fix it.** Then it offers Try Again.
home_faq_fail_a2: It never touches your own Finder backups.
home_faq_trial_a1: **Yes.** Trial mode puts on the same blocks, but you can remove them in Settings.
home_faq_trial_a2: To lock them for good later, plug the iPhone into the Mac once more. It does not need to be supervised again.
home_faq_undo_a1: **Not on the iPhone itself.** That is why it sticks. A locked profile comes off only in one of these ways:
home_faq_undo_item_erase: Erase the iPhone, then set it up as new or restore a backup from before you supervised it.
home_faq_undo_item_configurator: Remove the profile with Apple Configurator on a Mac.
home_faq_undo_a2: The app can add blocks any time, but it cannot loosen or remove one. **In trial mode**, remove the profile in Settings.
home_faq_apps_term: What happens to my other apps?
home_faq_apps_a1: **They stay.** Only the apps you choose disappear.
home_faq_apps_item_store: The App Store stays on, so you can still install and update apps.
home_faq_apps_item_rest: Every app you do not block, your bank app too, stays on the phone.
home_faq_see_term: Can anyone see or track my phone?
home_faq_see_a1: **No.** Supervision is a setting on the iPhone. It does not connect the phone to anyone. Nobody can control it from far away.
home_faq_see_a2: The profile is a fixed, signed file. Once it is on, nobody can change it or read anything back. The Mac app sends three things to this site: your list of blocks, once, to sign the profile (the site does not store it), one anonymous count when a supervision finishes, and a check for updates once a day.
home_faq_source_a1: **Yes.** The code is public on GitHub.
home_faq_source_item_mac: **Mac app:** AGPL-3.0. Anyone can read, use and change it. Anyone who shares a changed version must publish their code too.
home_faq_manual_term: Can I do it without the app?
home_faq_manual_a1: **Yes, with Apple Configurator.** The {guide} shows each step.
home_faq_manual_a2: That way **erases the iPhone** first. You set it up again as new, and only what syncs to iCloud comes back. On iOS 26 and older, the app does not erase it.
home_faq_other_platforms_a2: Windows and Android are not planned right now. It depends on interest.
home_story_people: I meet a lot of people, and I help many of them with their work. Most people's problems come down to one thing: not being able to do hard things. When I checked their screen time, I mostly saw 6 hours and more.
home_story_shot_friend_1: A friend's screen time: 6 hours 38 minutes a day on average, September 14 to 21
home_story_attention: I'm {aware} that {attention} is the most valuable thing we have. Billion-dollar companies build addictive feeds to take it, and our willpower runs out by the afternoon.
home_story_social: I'm not against social media. X and LinkedIn gave me real opportunities. Used on purpose, they're great. After a while, the feed starts to take more than it gives us.
home_story_path: This summer I read “{post}” by Stepan Parunashvili, about turning an iPhone into a dumbphone with Apple Configurator. It worked, but the App Store was off, my bank app broke and I couldn't scan a QR menu at a restaurant. So I wrote a guide that keeps the App Store on and blocks only the addictive feeds. It was too long and too hard for most people, and it erased their phone first. So I built a Mac app that does the same thing in a few minutes, without erasing anything.

ext_privacy_lead: The attention awareness extension hides addictive feeds with CSS. It collects nothing.
ext_privacy_stores_body: Your switches (on or off per website) and the custom CSS rules you write, in the browser's extension storage.
ext_privacy_stores_sync: If you are signed into your browser, the browser may sync that storage across your devices. Nothing else.
ext_privacy_sends_body: Nothing. No analytics, no crash reports, no remote code, no network requests of its own.
ext_privacy_sees_body: The pages on x.com, youtube.com and instagram.com, only to inject CSS.
ext_privacy_sees_custom: If you add a custom rule for another website, the browser asks you once for access to that website. The extension then injects your CSS there and nothing more.

guide_description: Supervise your iPhone with Apple Configurator on a Mac, then install a profile that blocks addictive feeds. It is free, and it erases the iPhone.
guide_title: Supervise your iPhone manually via Apple Configurator
guide_lead: The manual way to an iPhone without addictive feeds. Apple Configurator on a Mac supervises the phone, then a profile blocks the apps and websites you choose. It is free.
guide_erase_body: Apple Configurator can only supervise an iPhone by erasing it. Then you set it up again as new.
guide_erase_why_title: Why you can't just restore your backup
guide_erase_why_restore: A backup from before supervision brings your data back, but it also turns supervision off.
guide_erase_why_remove: Without supervision, the profile can be removed in Settings. On a hard day, the way out is one tap away.
guide_erase_why_apps: Without supervision, the profile can't block apps. It can only block websites.
guide_erase_icloud: So after supervising, only what syncs to iCloud comes back, like iCloud Photos, Contacts and Notes. Apps download again from the App Store.
guide_erase_backup: Back up your iPhone first, to iCloud or to your Mac in Finder. Restoring that backup is your way back if you change your mind. We are not responsible for lost data.
guide_erase_app: Do not want to erase it? On iOS 26 and older, the {app} supervises it without erasing, for free. It sends a small set of settings to the iPhone and restarts it, so your apps, photos and messages stay. Back up first for that way too. On iOS 27 the app cannot supervise the iPhone, so this guide is the way.
guide_need_mac: A Mac with macOS 15.7 or later, and a cable for your iPhone.
guide_need_passwords: Your iPhone passcode and your Apple Account password.
guide_step_backup_icloud: To iCloud: on the iPhone, Settings > your name > iCloud > iCloud Backup > Back Up Now.
guide_step_backup_finder: To your Mac: plug the iPhone in and tap Trust on it. Open Finder and select the iPhone. Under Backups, choose “Back up all of the data on your iPhone to this Mac”, tick “Encrypt local backup”, then click Back Up Now.
guide_step_backup_note: Keep this backup. It is your way back if you change your mind.
guide_step_erase_body: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings. Enter your passcode and your Apple Account password. This turns off Find My and Activation Lock, which Configurator needs. If your iPhone uses an eSIM and asks, choose to keep the eSIM.
guide_step_erase_stolen: If Stolen Device Protection is on and you are away from home, the iPhone asks for Face ID first.
guide_step_erase_hello: When the iPhone restarts, leave it on the Hello screen.
guide_step_configurator_body: Get {configurator} from the Mac App Store. It is free and made by Apple. Open it. If it shows a welcome screen, click Get Started.
guide_step_prepare_connect: Plug the iPhone into the Mac. When it shows up in Configurator, right-click it and choose Prepare.
guide_step_prepare_manual: Choose “Manual Configuration” and tick “Supervise devices”. Leave “Allow devices to pair with other computers” ticked. Leave “Add to Apple School Manager or Apple Business” unticked.
guide_step_prepare_skip: If it asks about device management, choose “Do not enroll in Device Management”. If it asks you to sign in to Apple School Manager or Apple Business, click Skip.
guide_step_prepare_org: For the organization, enter your own name. You are an organization of one. Then choose “Generate a new supervision identity”. Your Mac may ask for its password.
guide_step_prepare_setup: For Setup Assistant, choose “Don’t show any of these steps”, then click Prepare.
guide_step_prepare_done: Configurator erases the iPhone once more and brings it back supervised.
guide_step_setup_home: The iPhone opens straight to the home screen. In Settings, join Wi-Fi, and check Language & Region under General.
guide_step_setup_no_restore: Do not restore the backup from step 1. A backup from before supervision takes supervision off again.
guide_step_setup_account: In Settings, set a passcode and Face ID, and sign in with your Apple Account. What you sync to iCloud comes back on its own, like iCloud Photos, contacts, Messages in iCloud and passwords. Apps with their own backup, like WhatsApp, offer to restore it when you sign in.
guide_step_setup_find_my: Turn Find My back on in Settings > your name > Find My. It still locates the phone, but a supervised iPhone has no Activation Lock.
guide_step_setup_apps: Then install the apps you need from the App Store.
guide_step_setup_check: The top of Settings now says the iPhone is supervised.
guide_step_setup_managed: It also says “managed”. That is normal: no one manages the phone, because you skipped device management.
guide_step_build_body: Open the {builder}, pick the apps and websites to block, and download the profile. It is free.
guide_step_build_trial: The profile is permanent by default. Nothing on the iPhone takes it off. That takes erasing the iPhone, or Apple Configurator on the Mac. To try it first, tick Trial mode. A trial profile can be removed in Settings.
guide_step_build_by_hand: Configurator can also build a profile by hand, under File > New Profile, if you would rather set every option yourself.
guide_step_install_body: Unlock the iPhone first. Then drag the profile onto the iPhone in Configurator, or right-click the iPhone and choose Add > Profiles. A supervised iPhone usually installs the profile without asking. If it asks, open Settings and tap Install.
guide_step_install_done: The apps you blocked disappear, and the websites on your list stop loading.
guide_step_install_more: Forgot something? Build another profile and add it the same way. It adds to the one already there. A new profile can only add blocks. It cannot loosen one.
guide_undo_body: Erase the iPhone from Settings: General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings. That takes supervision and every profile off. Then restore the backup from step 1, or set it up as new. Anything you added since then comes back only if it syncs to iCloud. Apple Configurator on the Mac can also take a profile off a supervised iPhone.

open_description: The real numbers of attentionawareness.com, shown to everyone: visitors, page views, where visitors come from, Mac downloads and support clicks. Read from PostHog every 15 minutes.
open_lead: These are the real numbers of this site. Everyone sees what I see.
open_numbers_body: Only the live site is counted, and only as totals. Nothing here is about one person.
open_chart_title: Visitors and page views by day
open_chart_desc: Two lines from {from} to {to}. The most page views in one day is {top}.
open_track_posthog: The site uses PostHog. It counts page views and clicks, and it records visits. What you type is masked, and what you pick in the profile builder is hidden.
open_track_cookie: PostHog keeps a cookie in your browser, so one visitor is counted once. It does not store your IP address, only the rough place the address points to: country, city and postal code.
open_track_builder: The profile builder counts how many apps and websites you block, never which ones. To sign your profile, the list goes to this site once for each profile. The site does not store it.
open_track_openpanel: A second tool, OpenPanel, also counts page views and Mac downloads, and records one visit in ten. What you type is masked there too, and what you pick in the profile builder is left out.
open_track_iphone: Nothing on the iPhone is tracked.
open_track_mac: The Mac app sends one anonymous event each time a supervision finishes. It holds the app version, the method, and the first number of the iOS version and of the macOS version. Nothing in it names you, your Mac or your iPhone.
open_track_mac_updates: The Mac app also checks this site for updates once a day.
build_apps_body: It starts with the addictive feed apps people lose the most hours to. Search the App Store to add more.
build_description: Pick the apps and websites to block on a supervised iPhone, then download a signed profile. Free.
build_guide: Not supervised yet? {guide} shows how to get there.
build_install_1: On a Mac, open Apple Configurator and connect the supervised iPhone with a cable.
build_install_2: Select the iPhone, click Add, then Profiles, and choose the file you downloaded.
build_install_3: Keep the iPhone unlocked. A supervised iPhone usually installs the profile without asking. If it asks, open Settings and tap Install.
build_install_phone: Downloading on the iPhone itself? Tap Allow, then go to Settings > Profile Downloaded > Install.
build_lead: Pick the apps and websites to block, then download a signed profile. It goes on a supervised iPhone.
build_mac: The {mac} also installs profiles for free on any supervised iPhone.
build_stack_note: Every download is a new profile. A second one adds to the first and cannot loosen or replace it.
build_web_allow_body: Safari opens only the websites on this list and blocks everything else.
build_web_deny_body: Hiding an app leaves its website open, so every blocked app adds its websites here. Untick a website to leave it open.
gen_allow_app_store_help: Turning it off also stops app updates; banks and airlines break. Blocking apps by name is usually better.
gen_app_search_error: The App Store search did not answer. Try again in a moment.
gen_apps_empty: No apps blocked yet. Search above to add some.
gen_install_note: Blocked apps still download from the App Store, but they stay hidden and will not open.
gen_permanent_check: I understand this profile is permanent: it cannot be changed, and it cannot be removed on the iPhone itself
gen_sign_unavailable: Signing is not available right now
gen_trial_check: Trial mode: I can remove this profile later
gen_trial_help: Off by default. A trial profile can be removed in Settings. Turn it off and download again when you are ready to commit.
